newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram calls for punishing defaulters.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram calls for punishing defaulters.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Thursday urged swift punishment for those who exploit loopholes in the financial system, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
The news agency quoted Chidambaram as saying that quick punitive action must be taken against offenders.

"In a liberalised economy, most people would want to maximise opportunities while some exploit the system. While no one can stop crime being committed, there should be swift, severe and certain punishment for defaulters," PTI quoted Chidambaram as saying.
Chidambaram, addressing a seminar on the working draft of the Companies Bill, 1997, expressed his dissatisfaction with the present system.
"What is the use of a mechanism which falls flat on its face and people can thumb their nose against it," PTI quoted Chidambaram as saying.

Last month Indian financial markets were rocked by a scandal involving CRB Capital Markets, a firm that failed with thousands of investors' savings. The firm is accused of irregularities in financial services.
Indian federal police, investigating the collapse, estimate CRB's liabilities at 9.32 billion rupees ($260 million).
CRB chairman Chain Roop Bhansali was detained by the federal investigation agency on Monday.

Chidambaram said a meaningful standard of ethics for corporates must be evolved. He added it was impossible for any government to regulate nearly 400,000 companies, and urged the need for self governance.
"With corporate governance must exist an external regulation mechanism which must be clean, transparent and backed by an enforcement authority," he said.
Chidambaram said he believed a compnay's board of directors must not remain ornamental. The board, including government directors, should take responsibility, he said.
